themes.name: Nobody Can Verify Downstream
themes.plain: Once data, a message, or a dollar leaves your own systems, you cannot see inside the partner, ad platform, or trained model that now holds it. The best anyone offers is watching from outside: planting fake records and seeing what comes back, or expiring every list you send so nothing lives on by default.
themes.evidence: On provable downstream consent, deletion and purpose enforcement all three models said proof stops at the perimeter, with canary profiles and short-lived audience feeds as the honest substitute; the same ceiling shows up in cross-channel incrementality, where platforms control both the treatment and the evidence, and in ad supply integrity, where sellers report their own numbers.

themes.name: No Ground Truth to Measure Against
themes.plain: Most of these problems have no answer key. There is no trustworthy record of who is really the same person, what a model would have said anyway, or what a sale would have been without the ad, so the models start by buying or building a small truth set they can grade themselves against.
themes.evidence: Consent-aware identity resolution answers call accuracy claims unfalsifiable without a recruited panel, answer engine optimization answers say a model update moves the number more than a year of work, and B2B buying-group signal answers say a signal that decayed and a signal that was never real look identical.

themes.name: Chokepoint Before Trust
themes.plain: When the models cannot trust who is acting or what happens next, they build one door they own and push everything through it. A sent email, a spent dollar, or an exported list cannot be called back, so the only real control happens before the action leaves.
themes.evidence: Safe agent execution answers converge on a proxy or gateway with hard spend, rate and audience caps because sends and spend have no rollback; downstream consent answers cut direct credentials so every export passes one gate, and journey orchestration answers build a shared contact log that can only say no.

themes.name: Incentives Before Standards
themes.plain: Many of these problems stall because whoever holds the answer gains nothing by sharing it, and nobody can force them. So the models try to make honesty pay, or they stop waiting for cooperation and work only with what they already own.
themes.evidence: Agentic traffic answers build a fast lane with better prices so declaring beats spoofing, journey orchestration answers say channel owners are paid to keep sending, ad supply answers say the parties measuring fraud profit from the traffic, and semantic layer answers call definition conflicts a political settlement, not a modeling gap.

themes.name: Judgment That Won't Compile
themes.plain: The hardest calls turn on meaning and context: whether a picture next to a headline implies a promise, whether evidence really backs a claim, whether two teams can both be right about what a word means. No rule set captures that, so the models shrink human judgment into a smaller, safer box instead of removing it.
themes.evidence: Generative content governance answers build a registry of pre-approved claims because implied meaning cannot be checked by software, and semantic context layer answers say conflicting definitions of customer are legitimate, so the goal is forced disclosure of which definition was used rather than one true answer.
